questions.explain: Reactive scaling fails because detection, decision, and provisioning take minutes — capacity often arrives after the spike has passed, leaving over-provisioned resources idle.
options: Detection and provisioning take minutes, so capacity arrives after the spike has already peaked
Databases cannot be scaled at all
questions.q: Why does reactive scaling fail, according to the chapter?

questions.explain: The chapter recommends 90 days of five-minute samples to capture weekly seasonality and most monthly patterns without creating a storage burden.
questions.q: What is the recommended minimum telemetry retention for building a reliable seasonal workload profile?

questions.explain: Building a P50/P90/P99 workload profile by day-of-week and hour-of-day (e.g., with PERCENTILE_CONT grouped by DATEPART(WEEKDAY/HOUR)) is the baseline predictive model that requires no machine learning.
options: Compute P50/P90/P99 percentiles grouped by day-of-week and hour-of-day
Use only the most recent week of data
Require machine learning for any prediction
questions.q: What is the simplest, often most useful starting point for modeling workload patterns?

questions.explain: Pre-warming avoids the cold-start penalty by running intentional read queries against the most frequently accessed tables and indexes before a predicted peak, so hot data is already in the buffer pool.
options: Running intentional read queries against hot tables and indexes before the peak to load the buffer pool
questions.q: What is buffer pool pre-warming (cache priming), and how is it done?

questions.explain: Hysteresis requires the live workload to stay below threshold for 15–30 minutes before scale-in, preventing thrash when workload oscillates near the threshold boundary.
options: Scaling in immediately on the first below-threshold reading
Requiring the live workload to stay below threshold for a sustained period (15–30 minutes) before scale-in
questions.q: How should scale-in decisions use hysteresis to avoid thrashing between scale-out and scale-in states?
